newsitem.title: USA: N.J. school aid ruling prompts calls for amendment.
newsitem.headline: N.J. school aid ruling prompts calls for amendment.

text.p: New Jersey Republicans said they may try to eliminate the state constitution's "thorough and efficient" education requirement in response to a court order demanding more money for education.

Senate President Donald DiFrancesco said the legislature should consider a constitutional amendment that would get rid of the education guarantee, a clause in the constitution that has been the basis for 27 years of legal challenges to New Jersey's school funding system.

The most recent ruling came this week, as the state Supreme Court ordered the Whitman Administration to spend another $250 million on poor districts because the current school funding plan does not meet constitutional muster.

Another Republican, Senator Joseph Bubba of Passaic County, called the school-funding ruling another example of the court's "hopeless liberalism." Bubba introduced legislation that would require referendums every seven years on each justice.
State legislative leaders say they will find the money for the increase in aid to poor schools ordered by the court. But no decision has yet been made on exactly where the money would come from.
